parsed.explanation: The combined regime splits: the national layer imposes universal-exposure exposures (sex-at-birth passport policy affecting the country's own screening assumptions, a visa cable directing refusals where sex is doubted and fraud findings for 'misrepresentation', documented abuse of trans people in immigration and national custody, and facility bans in many sister jurisdictions), while this state/province layer is comparatively mild: no bathroom restriction as of April 2026, two protective city ordinances, a gender-identity hate-crimes statute, and a failed facility bill. The heaviest documented exposures are the entry/document regime and custody harm, both national and only partially remedied by pending litigation; the local layer adds minor-care denial for a travelling minor but otherwise little visitor-facing restriction. This sits at elevated, not reduced, risk: real recurring exposures with weak remedies, but not organised local targeting.

entry_documents.exposure: National visa cable directs refusal where sex is doubted and fraud findings for 'misrepresentation'; X-marker processing ended; reported passport confiscations and stranding; allied governments issued trans travel advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic; policy challenged in national courts; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign visitors' own passports normally govern, but visa adjudication and entry scrutiny apply to the visitor directly; screening can out a traveller at checkpoints.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted 2026 policies described as conversion therapy for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal); immigration-custody trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visa problem or entry dispute can route a visitor into national immigration custody where documented abuse occurred.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans in many other state/provinces; 4 make bathroom use criminal in circumstances; national order bars federally funded single-sex facilities by identity.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has no restroom restriction as of April 2026; two cities protect use by ordinance; a restrictive bill failed in the lower chamber.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facilities here follow identity in law and local ordinance; the parent rule governs national buildings only.

care_services.exposure: Minors: 2023 law bars gender-transition care for under-18s, upheld 2024 — a travelling minor cannot obtain care. Adult care availability not documented nationally beyond funding freezes.
care_services.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor cannot continue the minor's prescribed care here; adult visitor care is unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State government defines sex as assigned at birth and blocked marker changes; 2026 assessment ranks it among the most restrictive for trans adults; national rhetoric frames trans issues as ideology, counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No local criminalisation of presentation; proposals died in committee since 2021.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile state framing drives future bills; the national court has enjoined parts of the national programme.

minors_guardians.exposure: Under-18 care banned statewide; a 2023 law requires parental notification of a minor's chosen name/pronoun at school; one case saw a nine-year-old's bathroom access restricted by birth-certificate sex.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian of a trans minor faces care denial and school disclosure requirements; adult visitor unaffected.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented trans-specific street violence here; elsewhere one arrest under another state's bathroom law, not this one.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crimes law (2019) covers gender identity as sentencing enhancement; employment protections in several localities.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police recourse exists on paper; enforcement data not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Custody placement here undocumented; adult care availability undocumented; religious-freedom statute's gender-identity coverage unresolved; marker-ban litigation outcome unknown; more targeting bills pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation pending against national passport policy; state marker-ban challenged in court.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns leave entry questioning and detention placement unresolved; pending suits may change the regime either way.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar structure: no presentation offence or facility ban locally, documented visitor friction elsewhere in the system, partial remedies. This dossier's entry/custody exposures are heavier than Teravi's ferry refusals but the local protective layer (city ordinances, hate-crimes law) is comparable; overall near the same level.

0.35-B has a binding birth-sex placement rule reaching every detained or hospitalised visitor with no remedy. Here, custody harm is documented nationally but placement rules in this state/province are undocumented, and no universal state facility rule operates; hence this jurisdiction sits above that anchor.

0.75-C shows dead-letter law plus working courts and no custody open question. This dossier's national custody abuse and entry fraud ground are active, not dead-letter, and multiple open questions remain; it cannot reach that level despite the protective local layer.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime the visitor meets is a hostile national document and entry apparatus (sex-at-birth passport logic, a fraud-refusal visa cable, scanner and checkpoint outing risk) plus a documented record of trans abuse in national and immigration custody — these are universal or high-reach exposures with weak remedies, and allied governments' advisories corroborate real-world friction. Against this, the specific state/province is currently one of the safer local layers: identity-congruent restroom use is lawful, two cities protect it, a gender-identity hate-crimes enhancement exists, the worst bill died, and the exposure here for a travelling adult is mainly national, not local. The travelling-with-minor case is materially worse: an upheld care ban prevents continuing a minor's treatment, and school disclosure rules apply to resident contexts. Balancing tier-2 national exposures against a comparatively protective local regime with documented recourse gives an elevated-risk score, with custody and entry placement as the principal unresolved aggravators.
